iterations.strategy: Category B/C: data_loading was 58ms (72% of total) because MAP_POPULATE forced all 1.68GB to be faulted in, but zonemap skips 85% of blocks so only ~252MB is needed. Fix: (1) Remove MAP_POPULATE from all mmap calls — use plain mmap so pages are demand-faulted only when accessed. (2) After zonemap filtering, use madvise(MADV_WILLNEED) only on qualifying block byte ranges for all 4 columns to trigger async readahead for just the needed pages. (3) Use madvise(MADV_DONTNEED) or simply skip madvise on non-qualifying ranges. (4) Pre-compute the list of qualifying blocks from the zonemap in a single-threaded pass first, then distribute only qualifying blocks to threads via OpenMP parallel for. (5) In the scan loop, apply filters in order: shipdate (int32 range, selectivity 0.15) → discount (double range, 0.27) → quantity (double threshold, 0.46). (6) Use thread-local double accumulators with final reduction. This should reduce data_loading to near-zero (mmap setup only) and concentrate I/O cost into the scan phase where it overlaps with computation on qualifying blocks only.
